# Remediation Plan: From AI Agent Engineer to Robotics Algorithm Engineer

> **Important Note:**  
> The gap analysis reveals a fundamental domain mismatch. The resume’s core strength lies in LLM-based agent systems, while the job requires expertise in SLAM, robot perception, path planning, and embedded sensor fusion. **A successful transition realistically demands 6–12 months of intensive study and project work** to pass technical screens. This plan assumes the candidate is fully committed to a career pivot and can dedicate ~30 hours/week to learning.

---

## Week 1 (Urgent): Foundational Literacy & Quick Wins

These items establish basic domain vocabulary and make the resume *marginally* more relevant. They will not close the core gaps, but they show initiative and allow you to speak intelligently in networking conversations.

### Gap 1: No ROS/Robotics Fundamentals
**Priority:** High – ROS is the de facto framework for all JD‑mentioned algorithms (SLAM, perception, control).  
**Learning Resource:**  
- [ROS2 Humble Tutorials (official)](https://docs.ros.org/en/humble/Tutorials.html) – Focus on “Beginner: CLI Tools” and “Beginner: Client Libraries” (using Python first, then C++).  
- Read *Programming Robots with ROS* (Quigley et al.), Chapters 1–4.  
**Time Estimate:** 10–15 hours this week.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Build a simple ROS2 package that publishes/subscribes to a `/cmd_vel` topic in simulation (Gazebo/Webots). Add this as a “mini‑project” on the resume under a new “Robotics Foundations” section.

### Gap 2: C++ for High‑Performance Algorithm Development
**Priority:** High – All SLAM/perception implementations require C++ fluency.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- [learncpp.com](https://www.learncpp.com/) – Complete at least Chapters 1–11 (basics through classes).  
- Additionally, solve 5–10 exercises from LeetCode (Easy/Medium) in C++ to practice STL containers and memory management.  
**Time Estimate:** 15 hours.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Rewrite a small Python tool (e.g., the Text‑to‑SQL agent’s Tool Registry) in C++ using CMake. Mention “C++ (Modern C++17)” on the resume, with a note about active learning.

### Gap 3: Broad Robotics Terminology & Research Landscape
**Priority:** Medium – Necessary to understand interview questions.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- *Probabilistic Robotics* (Thrun et al.) – skim Chapters 1–3, 7 (SLAM), and 9 (Planning).  
- Read 3 blog posts: “How a robot vacuum cleaner navigates” (e.g., RoboRock or iRobot tech blogs).  
**Time Estimate:** 8 hours.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Write a 500‑word summary of “Key challenges in 2D LiDAR SLAM for domestic robots” and share it on a personal blog or LinkedIn. This becomes a talking point.

---

## Week 2–4 (Short‑term): Core Algorithm Competence

These skills are the **minimum** to survive an initial technical screen. After this block, you should be able to implement basic robotics algorithms.

### Gap 4: SLAM Theory & Cartographer
**Priority:** High – Explicitly required: “cartographer, 2D SLAM, 激光SLAM”.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- [Cyrill Stachniss SLAM course (YouTube)](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLgnQpQtFTOGQrZ4O5QzbIHgl3b1JHimN_) – Lectures 1–10 (EKF‑SLAM, Graph‑SLAM).  
- Google Cartographer documentation + hands‑on: Run Cartographer on a public dataset (e.g., [Deutsches Museum](https://google-cartographer-ros.readthedocs.io/en/latest/demos.html#demos)) using the ROS integration. Tune parameters and read the algorithmic paper.  
- Implement a tiny **filter‑based SLAM** from scratch in Python (1D robot with one landmark) to internalize the math.  
**Time Estimate:** 40 hours.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Create a GitHub repository: `mini‑slam‑demo` that contains your Python EKF‑SLAM implementation and a recorded Cartographer dataset run. Link it on the resume. List “Cartographer (ROS)”, “EKF‑SLAM fundamentals”.

### Gap 5: Robot Perception (LiDAR, Point Cloud, Obstacle Detection)
**Priority:** High – Required: “线激光、雷达、点云传感器、融合感知算法、避障”.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- [Coursera: “Robotics: Perception” by UPenn](https://www.coursera.org/learn/robotics-perception) – Weeks 1–3 (perspective, projective geometry, point cloud processing).  
- PCL (Point Cloud Library) Tutorials: [Basic Usage](https://pcl.readthedocs.io/projects/tutorials/en/latest/) – practice reading, filtering, and segmenting LiDAR data.  
- Use the **KITTI dataset** or a TurtleBot3 simulation: write a ROS node that subscribes to `/scan` and publishes obstacle bounding boxes.  
**Time Estimate:** 35 hours.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Build a “Laser‑based Obstacle Detection” project using ROS + PCL, visualized in RViz. Document the pipeline (crop, ground removal, Euclidean clustering). Mention “融合感知算法” after practicing with multiple sensor sources (e.g., lidar + depth camera).

### Gap 6: Path Planning & Control (A*, DWA, Coverage)
**Priority:** High – Required: “全局/局部路径规划、路径跟踪、动态避障、全覆盖”.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- *Robotics, Vision and Control* (Corke) – Chapters on path planning (A*, RRT, PRM) and robot control (PID, pure pursuit).  
- Implement A* and DWA from scratch in Python (grid world), then integrate with ROS: use the `nav2` stack in simulation to understand how planners and controllers interact.  
- For coverage: read the paper “A Survey on Coverage Path Planning for Robotics” and implement a simple boustrophedon planner in simulation.  
**Time Estimate:** 40 hours.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Create a “Coverage Path Planner for Rectangular Areas” ROS 2 service. Demonstrate it in a Gazebo simulation of a vacuum cleaner. This directly aligns with the JD’s “全覆盖” requirement.

---

## Month 2+ (Deepening & Specialization)

After the first month, you will have built a basic robotics foundation. The next phase focuses on **industry‑specific depth** and bridging the resume gap for competitive roles.

### Gap 7: Industry Experience – Sweeping/Vacuum Robots
**Priority:** High – “扫地机/商业清洁机器人经验优先”.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- Study the **RoboRock/Dreame tech white papers** (often publicly released on GitHub or blogs).  
- Participate in the **RoboCup@Home** or **Amazon Clean‑Up** simulation challenges (offline) to build realistic cleaning‑robot behaviors.  
- Build a complete **simulated vacuum robot**: integrate SLAM (Cartographer/slam_toolbox) → coverage planning → obstacle avoidance and auto‑docking with a virtual charging station.  
**Time Estimate:** 60+ hours (ongoing project).  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Produce a 5‑minute video walkthrough of your fully autonomous simulation. Add a detailed project entry to the resume: “Domestic Cleaning Robot Autonomy Stack (ROS2, Cartographer, Nav2)”. This is the strongest possible signal.

### Gap 8: Embedded & Sensor Integration (IMU, Motor Control, Dtof, Small FOV)
**Priority:** Medium – “imu电机控制、精度相关经验优先”.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- *Handbook of Modern Sensors* (Fraden) – chapters on inertial sensors, time‑of‑flight sensors.  
- Buy a cheap hardware kit (e.g., **Arduino + MPU6050 IMU + motor encoder**) and write C++ firmware that performs odometry fusion (EKF). This is crucial for understanding “融合里程计”.  
- For Dtof/small FOV: study the technical specifications of sensors used in Xiaomi/Dreame vacuums (often IR depth sensors).  
**Time Estimate:** 30 hours (hardware + software).  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Show a Kalman‑filtered odometry plot on a real robot (even a 2‑wheel chassis). Present it as “Sensor Fusion: IMU + Wheel Odometry EKF”. This directly addresses the “融合里程计” and embedded requirement.

### Gap 9: Image Processing & OpenCV on Linux
**Priority:** Medium – “精通opencv、SLAM建图后的图像处理”.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- *Learning OpenCV 4 Computer Vision with Python* (Géron) – focus on filtering, segmentation, and 2D image processing.  
- Complete a project: after SLAM, process the generated occupancy grid map to **clean walls, remove noise, and extract room polygons** (morphological ops, contour detection). This is exactly “建图后的图像处理”.  
**Time Estimate:** 25 hours.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Write a ROS node that subscribes to the `/map` topic, converts it to an OpenCV image, cleans it up, and publishes a refined map. Add to resume: “Post‑SLAM Map Refinement with OpenCV”.

### Gap 10: Advanced SLAM & Back‑end Optimization
**Priority:** Medium – “后端优化、回环检测”.  
**Learning Resource:**  
- *Introduction to Visual SLAM* (Ma et al.) – chapters on graph optimization, g2o library.  
- Implement a loop‑closure detection module using scan‑matching (ICP) in 2D laser data.  
**Time Estimate:** 30 hours.  
**How to Demonstrate:**  
- Open‑source contribution: fix an issue in a cartographer or slam_toolbox repository. Or create a stand‑alone loop closure detection library that can be plugged into your previous projects.

---

## How to Rearrange the Resume (After Completing at Least Week 2‑4)

To pass initial ATS filters, **the resume must be restructured entirely**. The current resume will not survive keyword matching. After acquiring the basics, create a new section:

```
## Robotics & Autonomous Systems Projects
• **Autonomous Vacuum Robot Stack** | ROS2, Cartographer, Nav2 (02/2026–present)
  - Designed a full autonomy pipeline: 2D LiDAR SLAM for map building, coverage path planning (boustrophedon), dynamic obstacle avoidance using A* and DWA, and auto‑docking.
  - Implemented laser‑based obstacle detection using PCL (Euclidean clustering) and fused IMU odometry for robust localization.
• **Post‑SLAM Map Refinement** | OpenCV, C++, Linux (03/2026)
  - Developed a map post‑processing node using OpenCV to denoise occupancy grids and extract room boundaries, used for cleaning pattern optimization.
  - [Include project links]
```

Then, repackage past experience as briefly as possible, highlighting transferable **engineering discipline**:

```
## Engineering Background
• Built distributed asynchronous task orchestration systems (100k+ tasks/day) with 99.9% uptime and robust monitoring (Prometheus, Kafka). This demonstrates real‑time systems mindset applicable to robot software reliability.
• Led end‑to‑end delivery of AI products from POC to production, practicing customer requirement analysis and cross‑team collaboration.
```

---

## Final Realistic Assessment

After diligently following this plan for 4–6 months (full‑time equivalent), your profile will be **competitive for entry‑level robotics algorithm** positions, especially if the simulation project is polished. However, expect to demonstrate deep understanding during technical interviews, not just project stitching. The original resume’s AI Agent experience will become a secondary story—use it to show you can ship complex software, not as domain expertise.

**Recommendation:** If you cannot commit to this intensive reskilling, it is more practical to pivot toward roles that blend AI Agents with physical systems (e.g., Embodied AI, robotics tool‑using LLMs) rather than a pure SLAM/perception role. That path would leverage your existing strengths more directly.
